chunks: From Abū al-Ḥusayn Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Asadī, may Allah be pleased with him, that there came to him, among what came in reply to his questions, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-ʿAmrī, may Allah sanctify his soul:

As for what you asked about regarding salat (prayer) at sunrise and at sunset: even if it is as people say, that the sun rises between the two horns of Shayṭān and sets between the two horns of Shayṭān, then Shayṭān’s nose is not humiliated by anything better than salat. So perform it, and humiliate the nose of Shayṭān.

key_terms.أَنْفَ: nose, used idiomatically for humiliation and subjugation
key_terms.الشَّمْسَ: the sun, whose rising and setting mark the times in question
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act of worship being asked about
key_terms.شَيْطَانٍ: Shayṭān, mentioned in the report associated with these times
key_terms.غُرُوبِهَا: its setting, referring to the sunset
key_terms.فَصَلِّهَا: so perform it, meaning the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) at sunrise and sunset in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of performing salat (prayer) at the times of sunrise and sunset. It states that even if common reports about these times are accepted, salat remains a superior act through which Shayṭān is disgraced, indicating encouragement rather than prohibition in this context.
